=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/clarify_data_provision_guard.py:90 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The section-header guard `stripped.upper().startswith("RATIONALE")` was changed from `startswith("RATIONALE") or startswith("EXECUTION PLAN")` to only check for RATIONALE. When the model emits `EXECUTION PLAN:` as a section header, `in_decisions` stays True and any single-letter Q-line inside that section would be mistakenly parsed as a decision.
  WHY: An EXECUTION PLAN section line such as `Q1: B` (a sample strategy label) could be parsed as a decision, overriding the guard's data-provision override with a wrong letter. The regex requires `[A-Z](?:\+[A-Z])*` ending at `$`, so realistic strategy tokens like `DERIVE_FROM_REPO` do not match; only a literal single letter like `B` could trigger this.
- scripts/clarify_data_provision_guard.py:83-94 | severity=NIT | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: The section-header detection uses bare `startswith("DECISIONS")` and `startswith("RATIONALE")` which do not match markdown-emphasized headers such as `**DECISIONS:**` or `**RATIONALE:**` or heading-formatted `## DECISIONS:` that models occasionally emit. When a bold header is used, `in_decisions` stays its initial value of True and never flips; all Q-lines everywhere in the output are parsed as decisions.
  WHY: A rationale line such as `Q1: B` inside a bold-headed RATIONALE section would be parsed as a decision, potentially picking a different option than the guard intended. As with the EXECUTION PLAN issue, realistic rationale text does not match the single-letter regex, so only a rationale that happens to be a bare letter would trigger.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

  PROBLEM: The section-header detection uses `stripped.upper().startswith("DECISIONS")` and `.startswith("RATIONALE")` after only a `line.strip()`.   WHY: The companion reader `auto_decisions.py::_answer_sections` already strips those via its `SECTION_RE` regex (`^(?:#{1,6}\s*)?(?:\*\*)?([A-Z]…)`), so the two readers disagree on what counts as a section header.
